description: Fig. 17 is a seven-panel composite mixing secondary-electron SEM micrographs of corroded low-density-steel surfaces with SKPFM surface-potential maps and a line-profile plot; no single modality dominates, so it is treated as composite. (a) SEM of S950 (5 µm scale bar) with a red box and dashed red lines marking the region shown enlarged in (a1). (a1) magnified SEM (1 µm scale bar): one grain is outlined in red, a yellow arrow labelled "grain boundary dissolution" points to the boundary and a green arrow labelled "intragranular dissolution" points to the interior. (b) SEM of S1150 (30 µm scale bar) with a red box marking the enlarged region in (b1). (b1) magnified SEM (15 µm scale bar) with the same red grain outline plus yellow "grain boundary dissolution" and green "intragranular dissolution" labels. (c) SKPFM map of ATBs (3 µm scale bar) with a red "Line A" crossing a bright band; the colour bar runs -30 mV (black) to 30 mV (white). (d) SKPFM map of HAGBs (2 µm scale bar) with a dashed blue "Line B" crossing a dark boundary; same -30 to 30 mV colour bar. (e) line profiles: Potential (mV, -20 to 20) versus Distance (µm, 0-12), Line A (red solid) and Line B (blue dashed).

subfigures.description: SE-SEM micrograph of sample S950 at low magnification with a 5 µm scale bar; faint grain boundaries are visible and a red rectangle plus dashed red lines indicate the region enlarged in (a1).

Magnified SEM (1 µm scale bar) of the red-boxed region of (a). One grain is outlined in red; a yellow arrow labelled 'grain boundary dissolution' points to the etched boundary and a green arrow labelled 'intragranular dissolution' points into the grain interior.

SE-SEM micrograph of sample S1150 at low magnification with a 30 µm scale bar; grain boundaries appear as faint etched lines and a red rectangle with dashed red lines marks the region enlarged in (b1).
Magnified SEM (15 µm scale bar) of the red-boxed region of (b); a grain boundary is traced in red, with yellow 'grain boundary dissolution' and green 'intragranular dissolution' annotations.

SKPFM surface-potential map showing an ATB as a bright diagonal band (high potential) in a darker matrix; a solid red arrow labelled 'Line A' crosses the boundary. Scale bar 3 µm; colour bar -30 mV (black) to 30 mV (white).

SKPFM surface-potential map showing a dark grain boundary (low potential) against a brighter matrix; a dashed blue line labelled 'Line B' crosses the boundary perpendicularly. Scale bar 2 µm; colour bar -30 mV (black) to 30 mV (white).

Line-profile plot of Potential (mV, axis -20 to 20) versus Distance (µm, axis 0-12). Legend: red solid 'Line A', blue dashed 'Line B'. Line A rises from about -10 mV to a plateau between the +10 and +15 mV gridlines; Line B remains near 0 mV but shows a sharp minimum close to the -20 mV gridline at roughly 6 µm.

observations.observation: Panels (a) and (a1) are SEM images of S950 and (b) and (b1) are SEM images of S1150; (a1) and (b1) are higher-magnification views of the red-boxed regions in (a) and (b) respectively.

The SEM panels show grain boundaries corroded into shallow continuous etching grooves with comparatively less dissolution in the grain interiors, annotated 'grain boundary dissolution' (yellow) and 'intragranular dissolution' (green) in (a1) and (b1).
Scale bars read 5 µm in (a), 1 µm in (a1), 30 µm in (b) and 15 µm in (b1).
Panels (c) and (d) are SKPFM surface-potential maps sharing a colour bar that runs from -30 mV (black) to 30 mV (white).

Panel (c) shows the ATB as a bright (high-potential) band with a solid red arrow labelled 'Line A' crossing it, and panel (d) shows a dark (low-potential) boundary crossed by a dashed blue line labelled 'Line B'.
Panel (e) plots Potential (mV) from -20 to 20 against Distance (µm) from 0 to 12, with legend entries 'Line A' (red solid) and 'Line B' (blue dashed).
In panel (e) the Line A profile sits at a positive plateau between roughly +10 and +15 mV, whereas the Line B profile dips to a sharp minimum near the -20 mV gridline at about 6 µm.

The caption states the figure shows dissolution behaviour of LDSs with different grain size at the initial stage of corrosion, with (a-a1) S950, (b-b1) S1150, and surface potential distribution for (c) ATBs, (d) HAGBs and (e) potential distribution.

The citing text asserts that ATBs exhibit a higher potential than the matrix while HAGBs show the lowest potential, making HAGBs the most electrochemically active and prone to preferential anodic dissolution.
The citing text attributes localised dissolution at certain ATBs to an approximately 30 mV potential difference between ATBs and the matrix, forming micro-galvanic couples.

The citing text states that preferential grain boundary dissolution during the initial corrosion stage creates favourable conditions for rapid oxidation of reactive elements such as Al, promoting an Al-rich oxide film.

Taken together the panels argue that the potential hierarchy ATB > matrix > HAGB, read off (c), (d) and (e), is what drives the preferential grain-boundary attack seen in the SEM panels (a1) and (b1).

measured_quantities: grain size (µm, sample context 8.7-32 µm per abstract)
unreadable_items: (a) and (b): individual grain-boundary grooves are very faint at the supplied magnification/resolution, so groove depth or width cannot be measured
